newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Zaire PM meets sick ruler Mobutu in Switzerland.
newsitem.headline: Zaire PM meets sick ruler Mobutu in Switzerland.

text.p: Zaire's prime minister, in Europe to discuss the conflict in eastern Zaire, has met his ailing president Mobutu Sese Seko during a visit to Switzerland, the Swiss news agency ATS said on Friday.

It said Kengo wa Dondo flew into Geneva on Thursday night and met Mobutu in Lausanne, 60 km (37 miles) east of Geneva, where the Zairean ruler underwent surgery for prostate cancer on August 22 and has since been receiving chemotherapy.

Some 300,000 Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees are on the run in eastern Zaire, fleeing clashes between Zairean troops and ethnic Tutsis. Concern is growing about the future of the vast, chaotic Central African country if Mobutu dies.

Kengo, in Belgium on Thursday, accused Rwanda of invading eastern Zaire to help Tutsi rebels. Rwanda denies the charge. The agency said Kengo, who arrived from Brussels where he had met European Union special envoy for the Great Lakes region, Aldo Ajello, left Geneva later the same evening.
The Zairean embassy in Geneva declined to comment.
On Thursday the Swiss foreign ministry extended Mobutu's visa on humanitarian grounds -- for the third time in two months -- but a spokesman would not say when it would expire.
The Swiss agency said Mobutu's new visa and those for more than 20 aides in his entourage would expire on November 27.
Fighting in the region broke out after Zaire's ethnic Banyamulenge Tutsis resisted attempts to drive them from their land and force them back into Rwanda and they fought back.

Western aid workers said on Thursday ethnic Zairean Tutsis fighting Zaire's troops were reported to have seized the airport in the eastern Zairean town of Uvira and cut off satellite and radio communications. The reports could not be confirmed independently.
